items.title: Transport across a moving control boundary
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume countable choice: every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $C_0\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $U_C$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline{C_0}$. Let $X\in C^2(I\times U_C;\mathbb R^3)$ have orientation-preserving diffeomorphic time slices onto open images (bijections with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant). Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous, and set $C(t)=X_t(C_0)$. Let $g$ be a scalar $C^1$ field on an open neighborhood of $\{(t,x):x\in\overline{C(t)},\,t\in I\}$. Define the boundary velocity by $w(t,X(t,\xi))=\partial_tX(t,\xi)$ and let $n$ be the outward Euclidean unit normal on $\partial C(t)$. Use Euclidean surface measure, whose chart density is $\sqrt{\det(DY^{\mathsf T}DY)}$. Then
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{C(t)}g(t,x)\,dx =\int_{C(t)}\partial_tg(t,x)\,dx+\int_{\partial C(t)}g(t,x)\,w(t,x)\cdot n(t,x)\,dS_x.$$
For vector-valued $g$, the identity holds componentwise. No condition equating $w$ with a fluid velocity is required.

items.title: Specified wall, thermal, periodic and initial data
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Work in the nonrelativistic SI fluid model on an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ measured in seconds and oriented Euclidean three-space measured in metres. Let $\Omega_t$ be the fluid region at time $t$ and $\mathcal O:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$ its open spacetime region. Let $u:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ be fluid velocity in metres per second, $T:\mathcal O\to(0,\infty)$ absolute temperature in kelvins, and $q:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ conductive heat flux in watts per square metre. A moving solid boundary is covered by local material surface charts $X_b:I\times\Xi\to\mathbb R^3$, where $\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is open with dimensionless labels and $X_b\in C^2(I\times\Xi;\mathbb R^3)$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives in $(t,\xi)$ of total order at most two are continuous. For each fixed $t\in I$ and each $\xi_0\in\Xi$, there is a neighborhood $V\subseteq\Xi$ of $\xi_0$ on which $X_b(t,\cdot)$ is injective, its derivative has rank two, and it is a homeomorphism onto its image; thus each time slice is locally a surface chart of the wall. These charts carry fixed material labels: wherever two such charts overlap, their labels are related by a time-independent $C^2$ coordinate change $\varphi$, so that $X_b^i(t,\xi)=X_b^j(t,\varphi(\xi))$ on the overlap. Differentiation in $t$ then gives the same velocity at each represented boundary point, and $w_b$ is the well-defined material boundary velocity $w_b(t,X_b(t,\xi)):=\partial_tX_b(t,\xi)$ in metres per second. For each $t$, every represented wall patch $X_b(t,\Xi)$ lies in $\partial\Omega_t$; locally this boundary is a $C^2$ graph with $\Omega_t$ on one side. Define $\Gamma_b:=\{(t,X_b(t,\xi)):t\in I,\ \xi\in\Xi\}$, taking the union over wall charts. The unit normal $n:\Gamma_b\to\mathbb R^3$ points outward from the fluid region $\Omega_t$ into the solid and is continuous. In the smooth branch, assume $u,T,q$ have continuous traces wherever boundary values are imposed. The no-penetration or impermeability condition is the adopted equality $(u-w_b)\cdot n=0$ on the wall. When separately selected, no-slip is the stronger adopted equality $u=w_b$ on the wall. Neither equality is deduced from an interior balance equation; no-slip is not part of the inviscid wall model unless explicitly adopted.

On a thermal patch $\Gamma_T\subseteq\Gamma_b$, a prescribed temperature is a map $T_b:\Gamma_T\to(0,\infty)$ and a prescribed outward heat flux is a map $q_b:\Gamma_T\to\mathbb R$. Require their pullbacks $(t,\xi)\mapsto T_b(t,X_b(t,\xi))$ and $(t,\xi)\mapsto q_b(t,X_b(t,\xi))$, wherever selected, to be continuous, with any additional regularity required by the chosen evolution problem stated separately. At each thermal boundary patch, select and state compatible data of one of these forms: insulation, $q\cdot n=0$; prescribed temperature, $T=T_b$ for a specified field $T_b>0$ in kelvins; or prescribed outward conductive heat flux, $q\cdot n=q_b$ for a specified field $q_b$ in watts per square metre. These are alternative boundary models. Their energy and entropy fluxes are accounted for through the chosen boundary data; no separate surface storage or reservoir entropy law is implicit.

A periodic cell with side lengths $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ metres is the quotient torus $\mathbb T^3_L:=\mathbb R^3/(L_1\mathbb Z\times L_2\mathbb Z\times L_3\mathbb Z)$. Periodicity identifies opposite faces by the corresponding translations and requires equality of the fields and of each derivative trace required by the selected evolution problem. Paired fluxes then cancel in cell integrals. These identified faces are not physical walls.

At an initial time $t_0\in I$, prescribe only the fields present in the selected model. Require them to satisfy the exact function-space regularity, positivity, differential constraints, constitutive state-domain restrictions, and wall or periodic compatibility hypotheses of the particular evolution result being used. For the weak formulation, adopt Countable Choice (every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function) and the restricted Euclidean Lebesgue spaces, almost-everywhere equality and integral conventions of the conservative weak-form definition. These conventions concern the weak initial data. In the weak formulation, initial data enter through the test-function initial term; that fixes a distributional initial datum but does not by itself supply a strong trace. This postulate selects model data only. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity improvement, approximation, or solvability for any initial-boundary value problem.

items.title: Material mass balance implies local continuity
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open reference region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ have orientation-preserving diffeomorphic time slices (bijections onto open images with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant), and satisfy $\chi(0,a)=a$. Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous; write $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$ and $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Let $\rho_0\in C^1(\overline B)$ and $\rho\in C^1(\mathcal O)$ be positive mass densities, where $\mathcal O=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$. Suppose that for every nonempty bounded open $V$ with compact closure in $B$ and $C^1$ boundary locally a graph with the region on one side and every $t\in I$,
$$\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho(t,x)\,dx=\int_V\rho_0(a)\,da.$$
Then the pointwise continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_x(\rho u)=0$$
holds throughout the balanced physical region $\mathcal O_B:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(B)\}$. The larger set $\mathcal O$ is only the ambient regularity domain; no balance outside $\chi_t(B)$ is assumed or concluded. This is a conditional deduction in the smooth material model and asserts no extension to weak fields or vacuum.

items.title: Integrable weak continuum balance and entropy adoption
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt the mathematical Countable Choice convention: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Use the complete Euclidean Lebesgue spaces, measurable maps, almost-everywhere equality and Lebesgue integrals of the conservative weak-form definition. This convention specifies the mathematical weak branch.

Work in a classical Cartesian inertial frame with SI units on a fixed open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and time interval $(0,T_f)$, where $T_f>0$ is measured in seconds. Write $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for functions whose absolute value is integrable on every compact subset. Let all fields be measurable functions of $(t,x)$ on $\Omega\times(0,T_f)$. Space-time integrals use the restriction of $\lambda_4$ to $\Omega\times[0,T_f)$, and initial integrals use the restriction of $\lambda_3$ to $\Omega$; both restrictions use their trace sigma-algebras. The displayed iterated notation uses the completed-product convention, with section integrals for almost every time, as in the conservative weak-form definition. Require $T>0$ almost everywhere wherever $q/T$ or $r/T$ is used. Let $\rho\ge0$ be mass density in kilograms per cubic metre, $u$ velocity in metres per second, $\sigma$ Cauchy stress in pascals, $b$ body acceleration in metres per second squared, $e$ specific internal energy in joules per kilogram, $q$ outward-positive conductive heat flux in watts per square metre, $r$ specific heat supply in watts per kilogram, $T>0$ absolute temperature in kelvins, and $s$ specific entropy in joules per kilogram kelvin. Set $E:=e+|u|^2/2$, use $t=\sigma n$ for traction and rowwise matrix divergence, and define the test-gradient by $(\nabla\psi)_{ij}:=\partial_{x_j}\psi_i$ and the Frobenius product by $A:B:=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$.

A test function is a $C^1$ function on $\Omega\times[0,T_f)$, compactly supported in space-time and vanishing near $T_f$; it may be nonzero at $t=0$. Let scalar test functions be $\phi,\eta,\zeta$ and vector test function be $\psi$. Adopt as a separate weak-branch model assumption that the displayed conservative variables, fluxes and sources below belong to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and satisfy the following identities for every indicated test function. Initial conservative data $\rho_0,m_0,\mathcal E_0,S_0\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represent initial mass, momentum, total-energy and entropy densities; the initial terms specify distributional data and do not assert a strong trace.

Mass balance, for every scalar $\phi$,

$$\int_0^{T_f}\!\!\int_\Omega\bigl(\rho\,\partial_t\phi+\rho u\cdot\nabla\phi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega\rho_0\phi(0,x)\,dx=0.$$

Momentum balance, for every vector $\psi$,

$$\int_0^{T_f}\!\!\int_\Omega\bigl(\rho u\cdot\partial_t\psi+(\rho u\otimes u-\sigma):\nabla\psi+\rho b\cdot\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega m_0\cdot\psi(0,x)\,dx=0.$$

Total-energy balance, for every scalar $\eta$,

$$\int_0^{T_f}\!\!\int_\Omega\bigl(\rho E\,\partial_t\eta+(\rho E u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q)\cdot\nabla\eta+(\rho b\cdot u+\rho r)\eta\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega\mathcal E_0\eta(0,x)\,dx=0.$$

Physical entropy inequality, for every nonnegative scalar $\zeta\ge0$,

$$\int_0^{T_f}\!\!\int_\Omega\bigl(\rho s\,\partial_t\zeta+(\rho s u+q/T)\cdot\nabla\zeta+(\rho r/T)\zeta\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega S_0\zeta(0,x)\,dx\le0.$$

Every conservative density, product, flux and source displayed in these tests is required to be locally integrable up to $t=0$, including $\rho u\otimes u$, $\rho E u$, $\sigma^{\mathsf T}u$, $q/T$ and $\rho r/T$: its absolute value has finite integral on every compact subset of $\Omega\times[0,T_f)$ in the relative topology, using its values for $t>0$. This condition assigns no point values at $t=0$ and asserts no strong initial trace. Interior test functions impose no boundary condition; walls, thermal exchange, periodic identifications and stronger initial trace conditions are separate data. This weak mass/momentum/energy adoption and the physical entropy inequality are not inferred for arbitrary discontinuous or vacuum states from the smooth balance postulate. The source term and the sign of the entropy inequality use the outward-positive heat-flux convention above.

items.title: Local smooth balances with continuous body sources
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open reference region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ have orientation-preserving diffeomorphic time slices (bijections onto open images with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant) and satisfy $\chi(0,a)=a$, and set $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$. Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous. Let $\rho:\mathcal O\to(0,\infty)$, $u:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$, $e:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$, $q:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$, and $\sigma:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ be $C^1$ on $\mathcal O$. Let $b:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $r:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Require $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$ for every $(t,a)\in I\times U$, so $u$ is the velocity induced by this same material motion. Their SI units are respectively kilograms per cubic metre, metres per second, joules per kilogram, watts per square metre, pascals, metres per second squared, and watts per kilogram. Put $k=|u|^2/2$, $E=e+k$, $D_xu=(\partial_{x_j}u_i)_{ij}$, $D=(D_xu+(D_xu)^{\mathsf T})/2$, $D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla_x$, and $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$. Use rowwise divergence $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$, vector divergence $\operatorname{div}q=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}q_j$, and traction $t=\sigma n$, where $n$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal and $q\cdot n>0$ denotes heat leaving the material region.

Assume pointwise mass continuity and, on every material region $P_t=\chi_t(V)$ where $V$ is a nonempty bounded open reference region with compact closure in $B$ and $C^1$ boundary locally a graph with the region on one side, the adopted linear-momentum, angular-momentum, and total-energy balances
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}\sigma n\,dS,$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}x\times(\rho u)\,dx=\int_{P_t}x\times(\rho b)\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}x\times(\sigma n)\,dS,$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho E\,dx=\int_{P_t}(\rho b\cdot u+\rho r)\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}\bigl(u\cdot\sigma n-q\cdot n\bigr)\,dS.$$
The angular balance is about a fixed inertial origin and there are no surface couples or intrinsic spin. Then throughout the balanced physical region $\mathcal O_B:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(B)\}$, with $\mathcal O$ retained only as the ambient regularity domain,
$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}_x(\rho u\otimes u-\sigma)=\rho b,$$
$$\sigma=\sigma^{\mathsf T},$$
$$\partial_t(\rho E)+\operatorname{div}_x(\rho E u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q)=\rho b\cdot u+\rho r,$$
and
$$\partial_t(\rho k)+\operatorname{div}_x(\rho k u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u)=\rho b\cdot u-\sigma:D,\qquad \rho D_t e=\sigma:D-\operatorname{div}_xq+\rho r.$$
Conversely, the pointwise momentum equation and symmetric stress imply the angular-momentum balance, and the pointwise total-energy equation implies its stated material integral balance. All deductions are conditional on the smooth model and do not assert existence of a solution.

items.title: Fluid conservation and entropy jump conditions
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Use the restricted complete Euclidean Lebesgue spaces, almost-everywhere identification and signed integrals of the conservative weak-form definition. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open spatial region and $I=(0,T_f)$ a time interval in seconds, with $T_f>0$. Let $\Sigma$ be a $C^1$ moving interface in $\Omega\times I$ that locally is the graph $x_3=h(t,x_1,x_2)$ and separates minus and plus sides; here $C^1$ means that the graph function and its first coordinate partial derivatives are continuous. Let $n$ be the dimensionless Euclidean unit normal pointing from minus to plus, and let $V_n$ be the signed normal speed of $\Sigma$ in metres per second. For a field with one-sided traces, define $[g]:=g_+-g_-$. Let $\rho\ge0$ be mass density in kilograms per cubic metre, $u$ velocity in metres per second, $\sigma$ Cauchy stress in pascals, $e$ specific internal energy in joules per kilogram, $q$ outward-positive heat flux in watts per square metre, $T>0$ absolute temperature in kelvins, $s$ specific entropy in joules per kilogram kelvin, $b$ body acceleration in metres per second squared, and $r$ specific heat supply in watts per kilogram. Set $E:=e+|u|^2/2$ in joules per kilogram. Assume these fields are $C^1$ on each side and, for every relatively compact interface patch, admit $C^1$ one-sided extensions to its closed sides; here $C^1$ means that the fields and all their first time and spatial coordinate partial derivatives are continuous on those extensions. In particular, the resulting one-sided traces are finite and continuous. Assume that all displayed products and sources are locally integrable. The sources are ordinary volume functions and have no measure concentrated on $\Sigma$. Use traction $t=\sigma n$, $(u\otimes u)_{ij}=u_i u_j$, and rowwise matrix divergence $(\operatorname{div}F)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}F_{ij}$.

On each side suppose the classical equations hold:

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,$$

$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u-\sigma)=\rho b,$$

$$\partial_t(\rho E)+\operatorname{div}(\rho E u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q)=\rho b\cdot u+\rho r,$$

$$\partial_t(\rho s)+\operatorname{div}(\rho s u+q/T)\ge\rho r/T.$$

Adopt the separate weak mass, momentum and total-energy identities and physical entropy inequality. Their interior restrictions use compactly supported $C^1$ tests in $\Omega\times I$, away from $t=0$ and $t=T_f$. The full weak forms may also use tests nonzero at $t=0$ and include initial-data terms; those terms are separate data and are not determined by the interface jumps. The interior weak conservation equations across $\Sigma$ hold if and only if the side equations hold and

$$[\rho u]\cdot n=V_n[\rho],$$

$$[\rho u\otimes u-\sigma]n=V_n[\rho u],$$

$$[\rho E u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q]\cdot n=V_n[\rho E].$$

For the entropy jump characterization, assume additionally that the vector field $q/T$ admits $C^1$ one-sided extensions to every relatively compact interface patch, with the same meaning of extension as above. This condition holds in particular if the temperature traces $T_\pm$ are strictly positive. It does not require positive temperature traces when the quotient itself extends; in that case $(q/T)_\pm$ denotes the trace of the quotient, not division of the separate traces. No extension or boundedness of the locally integrable source $\rho r/T$ is assumed. Under this additional flux hypothesis, the interior weak physical entropy inequality holds across the interface if and only if it holds on both sides and

$$[\rho s u+q/T]\cdot n-V_n[\rho s]\ge0.$$

Equivalently, for any conservative density $U$ and flux $F$ above, the interface coefficient is $[F]n-V_n[U]$. Here $[F]n$ is matrix–vector multiplication for momentum; for a scalar law its vector flux is identified with a one-row matrix, so $[F]n=[F]\cdot n$. The coefficient must vanish for conservation and be nonnegative for physical entropy. These conditions apply only to the specified piecewise $C^1$ fields and traces. They neither establish existence or uniqueness of a multidimensional shock solution nor extend smooth material equations through arbitrary nonsmooth fields.

items.title: Cauchy stress, local momentum and stress symmetry
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open reference region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ have orientation-preserving diffeomorphic time slices (bijections onto open images with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant) and satisfy $\chi(0,a)=a$. Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous. Set $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$. Use SI units in a classical Cartesian inertial frame with absolute time; inertial changes have form $t^*=t+t_0$, $x^*=Qx+ct+d$, where $SO(3)=\{Q\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3,\det Q=1\}$, $c$ is a constant relative velocity in metres per second, and $d$ is a constant spatial translation in metres. Let $\rho_0\in C^1(\overline B)$ and $\rho\in C^1(\mathcal O)$ be positive mass densities in kilograms per cubic metre, let $u\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^3)$ be the velocity induced by this motion, so $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$ for every $(t,a)\in I\times U$, measured in metres per second, and let $b\in C^0(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^3)$ be body acceleration in metres per second squared. Let $\sigma\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^{3\times3})$ be Cauchy stress in pascals, with traction $t(t,x,n)=\sigma(t,x)n$ for every outward Euclidean unit normal $n$. For every nonempty bounded open reference region $V$ whose closure is compact in $B$ and whose $C^1$ boundary is locally a graph with the region on one side, put $P_t=\chi_t(V)$. Adopt on each $P_t$ the material mass, linear-momentum and angular-momentum balances:

$$\int_{P_t}\rho(t,x)\,dx=\int_V\rho_0(a)\,da,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}t(t,x,n)\,dS,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}x\times\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}x\times\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}x\times t(t,x,n)\,dS.$$

Here $dS$ is Euclidean surface measure, with chart density $\sqrt{\det(DY^{\mathsf T}DY)}$. The angular momentum equation is about a fixed inertial origin; the model has no surface couples or intrinsic spin.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. The adopted traction representation is pointwise unique. The local momentum and stress-symmetry conclusions below hold on the balanced physical region $\mathcal O_B:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$; the larger $\mathcal O$ supplies ambient regularity only. With $D_tu:=\partial_tu+(D_xu)u$ and rowwise divergence $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$, the local momentum equation is

$$\rho D_tu=\rho b+\operatorname{div}\sigma,$$

equivalently

$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u-\sigma)=\rho b,$$

where $(u\otimes u)_{ij}=u_i u_j$. The angular momentum balance with no couples implies $\sigma=\sigma^{\mathsf T}$. Conversely, in this same smooth positive-density setting, the local momentum equation with symmetric $\sigma$ implies the angular momentum balance. The model postulate adopts the traction representation; this theorem establishes its local balance consequences and uniqueness.

items.title: Moving control-volume mass and momentum
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use a classical Cartesian inertial frame and SI units. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval in seconds, let $C_0\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $X:I\times U_C\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ family of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms (bijections onto open images with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant) on an open neighborhood $U_C\supseteq\overline{C_0}$. Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous. The moving control region is $C(t):=X_t(C_0)$; its boundary velocity is $w(t,X(t,\xi)):=\partial_tX(t,\xi)$ in metres per second. Let $\Omega_t$ be the open fluid region and $\mathcal O:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$ be open; assume $\overline{C(t)}\subset\Omega_t$ for every $t$. The fields $\rho:\mathcal O\to(0,\infty)$ and $u:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ are $C^1$, $b:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ is continuous, and $\sigma:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ is $C^1$. Their units are respectively kilograms per cubic metre, metres per second, metres per second squared and pascals. Let $n$ be the outward Euclidean unit normal and use Euclidean surface measure, with chart density $\sqrt{\det(DY^{\mathsf T}DY)}$. Set $(u\otimes u)_{ij}:=u_i u_j$ and $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. Use traction $t=\sigma n$. Assume the adopted single-component continuum mass and momentum balances in the following local material sense. For every $(t_0,x_0)\in\mathcal O$, there exist an open interval $K$ containing $0$ with $t_0+K\subset I$, a nonempty bounded open $C^1$ reference region $B$ containing $x_0$, an open neighborhood $U_B$ of $\overline B$, and $\chi\in C^2(K\times U_B;\mathbb R^3)$ with orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphic slices, positive Jacobian and $\chi(0,a)=a$. Require $(t_0+s,\chi(s,a))\in\mathcal O$ and $u(t_0+s,\chi(s,a))=\partial_s\chi(s,a)$ for all $s\in K,a\in U_B$. Write $\widetilde f(s,x):=f(t_0+s,x)$ for each field $f$. For every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with one-sided $C^1$ graph boundary, put $P_s=\chi_s(V)$ and let $\nu$ be its outward unit normal. Require

$$\int_{P_s}\widetilde\rho\,dx=\int_V\rho(t_0,a)\,da,\qquad \frac{d}{ds}\int_{P_s}\widetilde\rho\widetilde u\,dx=\int_{P_s}\widetilde\rho\widetilde b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_s}\widetilde\sigma\nu\,dS.$$

Assume also the Axiom of Choice. These material charts may depend on $(t_0,x_0)$; no global material chart or angular or total-energy balance is required.

Then every such $C(t)$ satisfies

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{C(t)}\rho\,dx=-\int_{\partial C(t)}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot n\,dS,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{C(t)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{C(t)}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial C(t)}\sigma n\,dS-\int_{\partial C(t)}\rho u\,\bigl((u-w)\cdot n\bigr)\,dS.$$

Only the normal component $w\cdot n$ enters these balances. If $C(t)$ is material, so $w\cdot n=u\cdot n$ on its boundary, the relative mass and advective-momentum fluxes vanish. The conclusion is a conditional model deduction; it asserts no existence of a flow satisfying the balances.

items.title: Kinetic/internal/total energy and boundary work
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open reference region with $C^1$ boundary (locally a $C^1$ graph with the region on one side), and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ be a motion with orientation-preserving diffeomorphic time slices (bijections onto open images with $C^2$ inverses and positive Jacobian determinant) and $\chi(0,a)=a$. Here $C^r$ means all coordinate partial derivatives through order $r$ are continuous. Set $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$. Use SI units in a classical Cartesian inertial frame. Let $\rho_0\in C^1(\overline B)$ and $\rho\in C^1(\mathcal O;(0,\infty))$ be positive densities, and let $u:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$, $e:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$, $q:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$, and $\sigma:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ be $C^1$, with $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$ for every $(t,a)\in I\times U$; let $b:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $r:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Their units are respectively kilograms per cubic metre, metres per second, joules per kilogram, watts per square metre, pascals, metres per second squared, and watts per kilogram. Define $k:=|u|^2/2$, $E:=e+k$, $D_xu=(\partial_{x_j}u_i)_{ij}$, $D:=(D_xu+(D_xu)^{\mathsf T})/2$, $D_t:=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla_x$, and $A:B:=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$. Use rowwise divergence $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$ and vector divergence $\operatorname{div}q=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}q_j$. For every nonempty bounded open $V$ whose closure is compact in $B$ and whose $C^1$ boundary is locally a graph with the region on one side, put $P_t=\chi_t(V)$ and let $n$ be its outward Euclidean unit normal. Use Euclidean surface measure $dS$ with chart density $\sqrt{\det(DY^{\mathsf T}DY)}$.

Adopt, on each such material region,

$$\int_{P_t}\rho\,dx=\int_V\rho_0\,da,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}\sigma n\,dS,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}x\times\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}x\times\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}x\times\sigma n\,dS,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho E\,dx=\int_{P_t}(\rho b\cdot u+\rho r)\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}\bigl(u\cdot\sigma n-q\cdot n\bigr)\,dS.$$

The angular-momentum balance is about a fixed inertial origin; assume no surface couples or intrinsic spin. Assume also the Axiom of Choice. On the balanced physical region $\mathcal O_B:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$, angular momentum gives $\sigma=\sigma^{\mathsf T}$, and the local total-energy balance is

$$\partial_t(\rho E)+\operatorname{div}(\rho E u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q)=\rho b\cdot u+\rho r.$$

It splits into the kinetic and internal-energy balances

$$\partial_t(\rho k)+\operatorname{div}(\rho k u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u)=\rho b\cdot u-\sigma:D,$$

$$\rho D_t e=\sigma:D-\operatorname{div}q+\rho r.$$

Thus the boundary power flux is $-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u$ and the outward heat flux is $q$. If additionally $b=-\nabla_x\Phi$ for a time-independent $C^1$ scalar potential $\Phi$ defined on an open spatial set containing every $\Omega_t$, measured in joules per kilogram, and $r=0$, then

$$\partial_t\bigl(\rho(E+\Phi)\bigr)+\operatorname{div}\bigl(\rho(E+\Phi)u-\sigma^{\mathsf T}u+q\bigr)=0.$$

Consequently $\int_C\rho(E+\Phi)\,dx$ is constant on any bounded fixed $C^1$ region $C$ with closure contained in the fluid region throughout $I$, with no-slip $u=0$ and insulation $q\cdot n=0$, or on a periodic cell $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j]$ with side lengths $L_j>0$ metres, $Q\subset\Omega_t$ for every $t\in I$, and opposite faces identified by translations when all fields and $\Phi$ are periodic. All local equations above are asserted on $\mathcal O_B$; the larger $\mathcal O$ supplies ambient regularity only. These are deductions for any solution with the stated regularity; the theorem does not assert that a solution exists.

items.title: Conservative momentum alone does not fix vacuum velocity
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Use the restricted Euclidean Lebesgue spaces and almost-everywhere convention of the conservative weak-form definition. On a fixed nonempty bounded open spatial domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and a finite time interval $(0,T_f)$ with $T_f>0$, the weak conservative mass and momentum equations, with the density, stress and body-acceleration fields held fixed and with fixed initial conservative mass and momentum data, determine at most one bounded velocity field up to almost-everywhere equality, even where the density is zero.
items.physical_scope: Formal weak mass and momentum laws do not determine velocity on vacuum; this is not a claim that a material fluid occupies vacuum.

items.title: Conduction preserves energy while entropy increases
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice: every set-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be side lengths in metres and let $Q:=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j]$ be a periodic cell, with opposite faces identified as in the periodic boundary-data model. Let $\rho>0$ be constant mass density in kilograms per cubic metre, $c>0$ constant specific heat in joules per kilogram kelvin, $\kappa>0$ constant thermal conductivity in watts per metre kelvin, $T_*>|a|>0$ a reference temperature and amplitude in kelvins, and $m\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$. Put $k_j:=2\pi m_j/L_j$ in inverse metres, define $k:=(k_1,k_2,k_3)\in\mathbb R^3$, and put $\lambda:=\kappa|k|^2/(\rho c)$ in inverse seconds. Choose $0<\delta<\lambda^{-1}\log(T_*/|a|)$, put $I:=(-\delta,\infty)$, and, for $(t,x)\in I\times\mathbb R^3$, define

$$T(t,x):=T_*+a e^{-\lambda t}\cos(k\cdot x),\qquad u:=0,\quad \sigma:=0,\quad b:=0,\quad r:=0,\quad q:=-\kappa\nabla T,$$

$$e:=cT,\qquad s:=c\log(T/T_*).$$

Then $T>0$, these fields satisfy the smooth balance equations on the periodic cell, and total internal energy $\int_Q\rho e\,dx$ is constant. The physical entropy density satisfies

$$\partial_t(\rho s)+\operatorname{div}(q/T)=\kappa\frac{|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\ge0,$$

and the total entropy $\int_Q\rho s\,dx$ is strictly increasing for every finite $t\ge0$. This is an exact conditional calculation for the stated balance-law and caloric model; it is not an experimental observation or a constitutive claim about a particular substance.
